title: Semantic versions
description:
Write the version tools a library and its callers need:

```cpp
struct Version { int major{ 0 }; int minor{ 0 }; int patch{ 0 }; std::string pre; };

bool parseVersion(const std::string& text, Version& out);
int compareVersions(const Version& a, const Version& b);       // -1, 0 or 1
bool compatible(const Version& builtAgainst, const Version& running);
std::string nextVersion(const Version& current, const std::string& change);
```

- `parseVersion` accepts `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with non-negative whole numbers and no leading zeros (except `0` itself), optionally followed by `-` and a non-empty label: `2.4.1`, `3.0.0-beta.2`. Anything else returns `false`.
- `compareVersions` compares major, minor, patch **as numbers**. With those equal, a version **with** a pre-release label is older than one without; two labels compare as plain strings.
- `compatible`: the running version has the same major as the one the program was built against and is not older than it.
- `nextVersion(current, change)` for change `"break"`, `"add"` or `"fix"` returns the next version as text, with no label: `1.6.3` + `"add"` is `"1.7.0"`.

```
compareVersions(2.10.0, 2.9.0) == 1
compatible(2.3.0, 2.5.1) == true
compatible(2.3.0, 3.0.0) == false
```
hints: Split off the label at the first `-` before looking for the two dots.
